audit.why: Emerald+ 46.55% over 797 games is the second-worst in the slice, and HARD at 7.5/10 matches it. The chart giving Jayce Levels 1-3 and Olaf everything from 6 onward is the honest shape of a lane a poke champion wins on paper and loses on contact.

Level 6 as the flip is right — Ragnarok is 100/90/80 and Jayce's R is the stance-swap he already had. The first-item and 2+ item calls are right too: Olaf's sustain scales with missing health, so it gets better exactly as the fight goes longer.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[2].text`, `wants.foe[2]`, `late` and `whys[5]` all attribute Olaf's lifesteal to 'his W (Vicious Strikes)'. Olaf has no ability by that name.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Olaf's W is Tough It Out — 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield', 16/15/14/13/12s, no lifesteal at all. His lifesteal is Berserker Rage, the passive: 'Olaf gains Attack Speed and Life Steal based on his missing Health.' That is not a naming nitpick, it inverts the advice. A W-based lifesteal would be a cooldown you could bait and then fight through; a missing-health passive is the opposite — it is strongest exactly when you have chipped him low, so poking him to 30% and then committing walks into his best sustain, not past it. The page tells the player to fight after the heal is spent, and there is nothing to spend.
audit.corrected: Berserker Rage (passive) gives lifesteal that scales with his MISSING health — his W is Tough It Out, an attack-speed shield on 16s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[1].text`, `mid` and `whys[4]` all say Ragnarok's true damage melts your no-armour frame. Ragnarok deals no damage.
audit.why: Riot's Ragnarok: 'Olaf passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' No damage component. The true damage in his kit is Reckless Swing — 'deals true damage to his target and himself' — 11/10/9/8/7 at 325 range. So the thing that ignores your armour is a short-range 11-second cooldown you can space, not an 80-100 second ultimate you have to wait out. Those are completely different problems with completely different answers, and the page merges them into one and gives you neither.
audit.corrected: Reckless Swing is the true damage, 11s at rank 1 and only 325 range; Ragnarok is the disable immunity, and it lasts only while he keeps attacking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ragnarok is described as flat CC immunity — 'makes Olaf CC-immune' — with no condition attached.
audit.why: Riot's wording is 'immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking'. The condition is the entire counterplay: Thundering Blow is not useless during Ragnarok, it is useless while he has a target to keep hitting. Knocking him back off everything, or breaking his attack chain, is what ends it — which is precisely the opposite of the page's instruction never to spend the knockback into an active R.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok's immunity holds only while he keeps attacking, so the knockback is not dead into it — it is how you break the chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block names Ragnarok and gives no number for it or anything else.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80 — the longest thing in the lane and the only cooldown genuinely worth waiting out. Undertow is a flat 9s at every rank and refunds part of that when he picks the axe up, so it is never a window. Reckless Swing is 11s at rank 1. The distinction between the 100-second cooldown you plan around and the 9-second one you simply space is the whole of the lane's sequencing and neither number is on the page.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok 100s at rank 1, Reckless Swing 11s at 325 range, Undertow a flat 9s that refunds on pickup.

edits.before: Ragnarok flips the lane. It makes Olaf CC-immune, so Thundering Blow (Hammer E) can no longer knock his all-in away, and its true damage carves through your zero-armor frame. Don't burn the knockback into an active R — bait it out or back off until it ends.
edits.after: Ragnarok flips the lane: 100s at rank 1, and he ignores disables for as long as he KEEPS ATTACKING. The true damage is not the ult, it is Reckless Swing (E, 11s, 325 range), which your armour does nothing against. Break his attack chain and the immunity ends.

edits.before: Once Olaf has first-item sustain, his W (Vicious Strikes) lifesteal out-heals your gate-Q chip, and his Undertow slow plus Ragnarok mean your Cannon-Q to Hammer combo can't kite back out. Your stance-swap speed keeps you alive but the trade math is now his.
edits.after: Once Olaf has first-item sustain, Berserker Rage's lifesteal out-heals your gate-Q chip — and it scales with his MISSING health, so chipping him low makes it stronger, not weaker. His W is Tough It Out, an attack-speed shield on 16s, not the heal.

edits.before: Drag fights past first item so Vicious Strikes lifesteal out-sustains the gate-Q poke while his true damage shreds Jayce's no-armor frame
edits.after: Drag fights past first item so Berserker Rage lifesteal — stronger the lower he is — out-sustains the poke while Reckless Swing's true damage lands

edits.before: First-item Vicious Strikes lifesteal out-heals your gate-Q, and Undertow plus Ragnarok mean your combo can't kite back out anymore.
edits.after: First-item Berserker Rage lifesteal out-heals your gate-Q and gets stronger as he drops, and Undertow plus Ragnarok stop you kiting out.

edits.before: Ragnarok makes him CC-immune so Thundering Blow no longer peels him, and its true damage melts your zero-armor frame — the level-6 window is his.
edits.after: Ragnarok ignores disables while he keeps attacking, and Reckless Swing's true damage melts your zero-armor frame — the level-6 window is his.

edits.before: - Olaf Ragnarok: matchup-defining — CC-immune — your knockback won’t hold him. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ragnarok: 100s at rank 1, and it ignores disables only while he KEEPS ATTACKING — break the chain and it ends. - Reckless Swing: 11s, 325 range, true damage. - Undertow: a flat 9s, refunded on pickup, so never a window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Undertow is a flat 9s and he refunds it by picking the axe up.

notes: Two independent factual errors, both repeated across four strings: Olaf's W is Tough It Out (attack speed and a shield), not 'Vicious Strikes', and his lifesteal is the Berserker Rage passive scaling off MISSING health; and Ragnarok deals no damage at all — the true damage is Reckless Swing (E). Both corrections push the same way, which is why they matter: the page tells you to chip Olaf down and then commit, and both facts say chipping him down is what turns his sustain on. `mid` and `late` still carry the same two errors in longer form; I corrected the spikes, whys and wants that state them most directly, but a follow-up pass on those two paragraphs is worth doing. Point 4 on Ragnarok's attacking condition is Medium confidence: Riot's wording is 'for as long as he keeps attacking', which I have stated as-is, but I could not verify from the kit files what exactly counts as an attack for that check or whether there is a grace period, so I did not tell the player to rely on the knockback breaking it — only that the immunity is conditional.
